findings.reason: two nodes hold opposite endpoints for one module with no order declared between them, so one lane is guaranteed to build work that is either dead code or aimed at an absent module.
findings.text: §10's clause (1) and (3) make the batched labeller and the reduced-Newton route the units to migrate and to re-verify, but §6's retirement (`plan.html:97`) deletes `reduced_newton.py` outright and the 2026-10-05 consumer ruling carried in §6 (`plan.html:783`) says the labeller re-points onto `solve.fixed_point` under `jax.vmap` before `reduced_newton.py` is deleted, "never a reason to keep the reduced-Newton route alive beside the new solve"; §10 declares depends-on `s8` only, so whichever of §6 and §10 lands second either migrates a module the other deleted or re-verifies receipts for code the plan exists to remove

findings.reason: the clause is the section's only numeric floor, so an unreferenced receipt turns the whole gate into a judgement call.
findings.text: the added clause asks for "their recorded tolerances" without naming the receipt the tolerance is recorded in or the tolerance itself, so "reproduces within its recorded tolerance" cannot be checked by a reader and a worker must guess which record is meant

findings.reason: §7 is the one gate every acceptance row and the receipt call, so an incomplete enumeration sends the node to a predicate that under-measures rows the later sections will be judged on.
findings.text: §7's clause (1) says the predicate evaluates "the clauses that apply to a row" and then lists four families, but §9 clause 2 requires the WEST 62751 row to show "zero cells changing support between the last two map applications" and report its boundary class (`plan.html:109`), and §6's table lists compiled programs per mesh shape, executable size, compile wall, host memory and tracing as clauses of that same gate; the predicate built from §7's list therefore cannot score the WEST row's stated acceptance or the compile-cost clauses §6 declares part of the joint acceptance

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §7's §4 and §6 references resolve, and §10's `f-cfs-legacy-read-migration` anchor resolves as the open followup at `plan.html:398`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §10's clause (3) requires "the batched labeller's and the reduced-Newton route's recorded receipts [to] reproduce within their recorded tolerances at the head" but names neither the receipt nor where its tolerance is recorded, so a worker cannot tell which run to reproduce or against what bound.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — neither reviewed unit places evidence on a temporary or node-local path; §10's floors are the paired suite logs the run records and the receipts it cites.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, ticket numbers, version tags or changelog prose in either unit.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §7 (`plan.html:101`) enumerates the predicate's clauses as global residual, constraint rows, null positions and map fidelity, omitting the support-stability clause §9 clause 2 makes a WEST acceptance (`plan.html:109`) and the compile-cost and tracing clauses §6's table lists as part of the same gate (`plan.html:80`-`84`).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §7 delivers one predicate and §10 delivers one migration-and-deferred-deletion, each with a single verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §10 (`plan.html:113`) migrates the reduced-Newton route and requires its receipts to reproduce, while §6's retirement (`plan.html:97`) deletes `reduced_newton.py` and the 2026-10-05 consumer ruling (`plan.html:783`) re-points the labeller onto `solve.fixed_point`; no relationship records which node owns that artifact or which runs first.
